Ayesha —

Appreciate the clear asks. I drafted a short proposal and attached a draft "sealed snapshot deposit" workflow and an ops runbook template. High level:
- We can provide a sealed snapshot (immutable archive + signed manifest) deposited with a neutral third-party custodian and a periodic witness test window (read-only verification).
- License scope: include an addendum that grants execution rights to the customer for the snapshot under defined termination scenarios; Redwood retains production model IP and runtime licensing as usual.
- Operator credentials: propose a temporary, time-boxed operator token for the witness rehearsal; long-term operator access remains governed by the Order Form exhibit and operator SLA.
- Acceptance rehearsal: a two-hour runbook-led session where the customer performs read-only verification and signs an acceptance report.

I've attached the proposal and a sample runbook. Can you confirm which stakeholders (legal/security) we should loop in on your side?

Regards,
Nikhil Sharma

Subject: INTERNAL: draft redlines for MSA addendum (sealed deposit, license carveouts)

Nikhil — quick internal note before we send to Aegis legal. I reviewed the sealed-snapshot proposal and put redlines into the MSA addendum (see attached). Key points:
- License carveout: allow customer execution rights for the snapshot only for continuity/forensic purposes; explicitly prohibit derivative model training or rehosting outside agreed environments.
- Custodian obligations: limit Redwood liability for custodian custody; require mutually agreed custodian with SLAs; no escrow provider that mandates source-code delivery.
- Rehearsal scope: define a single acceptance rehearsal per renewal period by default; additional rehearsals billable at a stated rate.
- Evidence retention window: propose 24 months retention for manifests and signed proof-of-deposit; longer retention to be a commercial add-on.

I'll attach the redline PDF and a short cover note to send to Aegis. If you want, I can propose alternate language to keep the license carveouts narrower.

Marissa Cole
Director, Legal Operations, Redwood Inference
